title: Stepped Capacity Preservation Controller and Autoscaler Interlock for Dedicated GPU Pools
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Upgrading dedicated GPU pools currently causes transient capacity shortages or sudden hitting of autoscaler limits when nodes are cordoned and drained, which leads to increased tail latency for production customers. Existing rollout controllers are aggressive and rely on fleet-wide drains that do not coordinate with the cluster autoscaler booking.

Goal: Implement a 'Stepped Capacity Preservation Controller' (SCPC) that performs controlled, windowed upgrades for GPU pools. SCPC will: (1) reserve a configurable headroom budget per pool, (2) perform stepped/epoch-based node reboots/drains using a token lease to limit concurrent evictions, and (3) interlock with the cluster autoscaler via a handshake API so autoscaler actions respect the upgrade window and avoid capacity over-commit. The solution must support LTS channel rollouts and be able to safely pause/abort on quality/regression signals.
acceptance_criteria: Controller can perform an upgrade on a 200-node pool without causing requests to hit 95th-percentile latency SLO increases above 15%
Autoscaler interlock API prevents scale-downs that would violate the reserved headroom during upgrade epochs
Can configure per-pool headroom percentage and max-concurrent-evictions settings via pool CRD
Supports canary -> staggered -> broad phases with automatic pause on error thresholds
A rollout runbook and rollback playbook exist and are validated in staging
design_decisions: Use lease-based tokens (Kubernetes Leases) to limit concurrent eviction tokens per pool instead of a centralized lock service to reduce blast radius
Headroom is expressed as a percentage of pool capacity and enforced by a two-way handshake with autoscaler (UpgradeController posts planned-evictions; Autoscaler replies with allowed-evictions)
Stepped epochs: default epoch length 10 minutes with configurable parallelism; epochs allow warmup of KV caches and rebalancing between waves
Controller will prefer graceful draining with prefetch of hot KV prefixes and application-level graceful shutdown hooks where supported
Abort semantics: controller records signals to a Rollout CRD; if error threshold exceeded, it pauses and emits diagnostics for manual intervention
rollout_plan: Alpha: deploy SCPC to staging dedicated cluster, run synthetic load tests and canary upgrades on single small pool (3-10 nodes)
Beta: enable SCPC in one non-critical prod region with conservative headroom (25%) and epoch parallelism 1 for 2 weeks
Gradual increase: after validated metrics, move to two regions and reduce headroom incrementally to 15%
Full: enable for LTS channel upgrades with default headroom 10% and epoch parallelism tuned by pool size
Emergency abort: onboard SRE runbook and automated rollback job that reverses cordon and re-enables nodes if pause condition met
metrics: p95 latency change during upgrades (per-route, per-model)
risks: If headroom set too low, autoscaler may be unable to provision replacement capacity quickly enough leading to customer impact
Handshake API adds coupling between controller and autoscaler; miscoordination bugs could lead to deadlocks if not carefully timeboxed
Lease churn in large fleets could add control-plane load; must instrument and rate-limit lease renewals
Edge-case: heterogeneous pools with mixed GPU types may require per-instance headroom tuning
Operational complexity: operators must understand headroom trade-offs vs rollout speed
